claims.text: Convex hull analysis of response embeddings can measure the dispersion and variability of LLM outputs for uncertainty quantification.
The uncertainty of LLMs depends on prompt complexity.
The uncertainty of LLMs depends on the specific model used.
The uncertainty of LLMs depends on the temperature setting.

evidence.description: The proposed method leverages the spatial properties of response embeddings to measure the dispersion and variability of model outputs.
The experimental results indicate that the uncertainty of the model for LLMs depends on the prompt complexity.
The experimental results indicate that the uncertainty of the model for LLMs depends on the model.
The experimental results indicate that the uncertainty of the model for LLMs depends on the temperature setting.

methodologies.name: Convex Hull Analysis of Response Embeddings
methodologies.description: Transforms LLM responses into BERT embeddings, projects them to 2D via PCA, clusters them with DBSCAN, and computes convex hulls to measure output dispersion.

limitations.text: Traditional methods for uncertainty quantification, such as probabilistic models and ensemble techniques, face challenges when applied to the complex and high-dimensional nature of LLM-generated outputs.
